question: wiki/open-questions.md item 6: gates on hmm_drive_0 (second-mode start) and lotka_volterra (starts on the rk45 failure boundary) are decided by the uniform(-2,2) start lottery. Does a cheap init-time rule remove the lottery without hurting anything?
change_under_test: New opt-in variant owalnuts::sampler::Init::Candidates { radius, candidates, max_attempts, selection: StartSelection } and owalnuts::sampler::candidate_starts. Per chain, `candidates` evaluable starts are drawn exactly as Init::Uniform draws one (same RNG stream; candidates = 1 reproduces Init::uniform() starts bit for bit) and one is kept by its log density. Init::uniform() and Init::Given are unchanged; the default is unchanged.

arms.default: Init::uniform(): uniform(-2,2) unconstrained, up to 100 draws per chain until log density and gradient are finite
arms.best16: arm A: Init::best_of(16) = Init::Candidates { radius 2, candidates 16, max_attempts 100 per candidate, selection HighestDensity }
arms.median16: arm C: Init::median_of(16) = Init::Candidates { radius 2, candidates 16, max_attempts 100 per candidate, selection MedianDensity (the (k-1)/2-th smallest, lower median) }

arm_not_run: arm B (best-of-16 with a gradient-norm feasibility margin) is not run: a highest-density candidate essentially never has a gradient norm many times the pool median, so B would reproduce A on almost every cell and the second arm slot is more informative spent on the opposite hedge (C).
common: Sampler at the shipped defaults: Tuning::default() (h0 0.5, depth 10, eight refinement levels, delta 1, MomentumSum), Metric::diagonal() with Stan regularisation, Adaptation::default() (dual averaging 0.8, no chain rescue), Limits::admit_worst_case(), 4 chains x 1,000 warmup / 1,000 retained, 4 threads; owalnuts-bridgestan ReplicatedStanTarget (BridgeStan 2.9.0, no STAN_THREADS)
init_cost_accounting: Every init evaluation (rejected non-finite draws included) is a full log-density-and-gradient call and is counted in gradients_total. The default arm's start log densities are measured afterwards with one extra evaluation per chain that is subtracted from gradients_total.
seeds_verified_unused: git grep -w over the whole repository (artifacts included) at 3583d130 finds no occurrence of 943101-943105; no sibling worktree protocol or preregistration names them.
run_order: models in listed order; within a model seeds ascending; within a seed arms default, best16, median16; strictly sequential, one child process per model and one harness process per cell; then the funnel row (seeds ascending, arms in order)
parameter_set: columns of the posteriordb reference draws; draws constrained through BridgeStan with transformed parameters included
estimators: ArviZ 0.23.4 rank R-hat, bulk ESS, tail ESS at 0.05/0.95, mean MCSE (posteriordb_bench_v6 functions reused verbatim)

hidden_mode.definition: a cell whose max rank R-hat <= 1.01 but whose mean on some reference parameter is more than 3 reference SD from the posteriordb reference mean
hidden_mode.scope: evaluated on every cell of every arm; hmm_drive_0 is the named target
hidden_mode.credit: a hidden-mode cell is never a credited pass, and ranks below a visible R-hat failure (outcome rank 0 < 1)

chain_mode.rust: owalnuts::diagnostics::ChainDisagreement on the unconstrained draws (leave-one-chain-out max R-hat; chains whose removal brings it <= 1.01)
chain_mode.reference_distance: per chain, max over reference parameters of |chain mean - reference mean| / reference SD; a chain above 3 is 'off reference' (ended in a different mode)

per_cell_record: each chain's start position and start log density, every candidate log density and the chosen index, init evaluations, gates, credited pass, hidden-mode flag, ChainDisagreement, per-chain reference distance, min bulk ESS per gradient (gradients include init), divergences, frozen chains, final steps
efficiency: per cell min over reference parameters of bulk ESS / gradients_total; per model the geometric mean over seeds where both the rule arm and default are ok; ratio rule/default per model; overall geometric mean of the 17 per-model ratios

funnel.target: Neal's 10-D funnel at the sampler defaults (no rescue); exact P(omega < -5) = 0.0478
funnel.starts: default: the house starts omega in {-3,-1,1,3}, x = 0; rule arms: 16 candidates per chain from uniform(-3,3)^10 (the house starts' largest |omega| is the pool's ceiling), chosen by the arm's selection via candidate_starts
funnel.statistic: per-seed MCSE z of P(omega < -5) (gate |z| <= 2 every seed), batch-means z reported, omega bulk ESS and R-hat reported

decision_rule.text: Recommend a rule arm as the new default iff (D1) its credited passes over the 85 cells >= the default arm's, (D2) it has zero hidden-mode cells, (D3) its geomean ESS/gradient ratio vs default >= 0.97, and (D4) its funnel |z| <= 2 on every one of the five seeds. If both arms qualify, recommend the one with more credited passes, then the higher geomean ratio. Otherwise keep Init::uniform() as the default. This study does not change the default: it ships only the opt-in variant; a recommendation is acted on by the coordinator.

predictions.P1: default: 70 to 74 credited passes of 85 (v5/WP34 rate 42/51, WP39B 44/51); centered eight schools fails 5/5, accel_gp 2-3/5
predictions.P2: the lottery: default has an off-reference (second-mode) hmm_drive_0 chain on 1-2 of 5 seeds; best16 on 0 of 5; best16 passes lotka_volterra 5/5
predictions.P3: best16 credited passes exceed default by 1 to 3
predictions.P4: best16 has zero hidden-mode cells (the second mode found from best-of-16 starts, if any, is visible to R-hat)
predictions.P5: best16 geomean ESS/gradient ratio vs default is in [1.00, 1.15] (init cost <= 0.1% of gradients; the gain comes from removed lottery cells)
predictions.P6: median16 is indistinguishable from default: credited passes within +-1, geomean ratio in [0.97, 1.03], and it still draws at least one off-reference hmm_drive_0 seed
predictions.P7: funnel |z| <= 2 on all five seeds for all three arms
predictions.P8: best16's median start log density exceeds default's on all 17 models
predictions.P9: mechanical decision: best16 qualifies and median16 does not

rules: Preregistration committed before the first evidence cell. Report all cells; no result-driven reruns; failures are results; nothing tuned after seeing results. A process crash may be relaunched and only a cell without a completed artifact may be run, with the deviation recorded. Walls are contended (nine sibling agents on 16 cores) and are not evidence.
